protocol.question: Does age ordering add benefit beyond redispatch itself?
protocol.design: Three policies; identical fixed redispatch clock for both redispatch policies
protocol.candidate_calls: All pending hall calls; onboard destinations and in-flight targets retained
protocol.age_definition: Earliest arrival of a passenger still waiting in this hall call
protocol.neutral_order: Age-independent seeded permutation of floor/direction keys at each clock tick
protocol.primary_outcome: Mean of per-run P95, after averaging neutral order replicates within each demand run
protocol.cohort_definition: Top ceil(5% * N) longest-waiting passenger IDs under ETA, fixed across policies
protocol.failure_definition: Rejection at an actual stop; full-car bypass not counted

bootstrap.unit: Demand-run pair after averaging order replicates

limitations: Conditional on simplified inherited boarding, movement, and ETA information model
Fixed-clock age_order_eta differs from historical age-triggered priority_eta
Neutral policy averages a finite set of random order streams
ETA-defined long-wait cohort is descriptive, selected using its baseline outcome
Floor summaries average runs with observed arrivals, not equally weighted passengers
